rationale: The speaker quotes the opening of the Constitution in quotation marks and calls it "the preamble to this Constitution".

from_quote: That no state, without its consent, shall be deprived of its equal suffrage in the Senate
rationale: The speaker quotes the proviso in quotation marks as part of "the articles respecting amendments".

from_quote: the senators, sir,—those tyrants that are to devour the legislatures of the states,—are to be chosen by the state legislatures themselves
rationale: The speaker describes the clause by which the senators are chosen by the state legislatures; no number is given.

from_quote: The President of the United States is to be chosen by electors appointed in the different states, in such manner as the legislature shall direct
rationale: The speaker describes the clause on electors appointed in each state in such manner as the legislature directs; no number is given.

from_quote: The judges are to be nominated by the President, and appointed by him, with the advice and consent of the Senate
rationale: The speaker describes the appointment of judges by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate; no number is given.

from_quote: The times, places, and manner, of holding elections for senators and representatives, shall be prescribed in each state by the legislature thereof; but the Congress may at any time, by law, make or alter such regulations, except as to the places of choosing senators
rationale: The speaker reads the clause in quotation marks and calls it "the fourth section of the first article".
to_quote: The Times, Places and Manner of holding Elections for Senators and Representatives, shall be prescribed in each State by the Legislature thereof; but the Congress may at any time by Law make or alter such Regulations, except as to the Places of chusing Senators

from_quote: By this clause, the times, places, and manner of holding elections, shall be prescribed in each state, by the legislature thereof
